verdict: Avoid new fruit & vegetable processing exposure in Nagpur for now; lend only to frozen/snack processors with contracted volumes and clean FDA records, and only with tight structure.
title: Nagpur Fruit & Vegetable Processing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A processor buys seasonal produce at harvest, converts it into pulp, frozen vegetables, snacks or gherkins, and sells into domestic FMCG or export channels. **Cash is made in the conversion spread, not in the crop** — raw material is the largest cost line [9], so margin lives or dies on procurement price and recovery yield. Working capital is the whole game: inventory sits from harvest to dispatch, and export receivables stretch further. **So when a proposal lands, check the inventory-and-receivable cycle against the crop calendar first; if stock days exceed one season, ask what is pledged and to whom.**

## What has changed now
Two signals point the same way. India-wide exports are down 9.6% Apr-to-date in USD [D], and the peer read-across confirms it: Foods & Inns reported realisations down 25.3% with Middle East disruption hitting cash flows [4]. **So when a proposal lands, check the export share of sales; if above a third, ask for buyer-wise order confirmation and past-dueness on export bills.** Locally, Maharashtra electricity demand is growing 3.5 pp slower than India [D] — a soft local demand signal — while GST collections run 2.5 pp faster than India [D], which tells us formal local trade is still billing. **Treat the GST number as the honest one and the power number as the warning.**

## The local picture is thin
Nagpur-specific evidence is limited to one enforcement item: an FDA raid seizing 15 tonnes of suspected noodles and maida worth about Rs 7 lakh [1]. **That is a compliance signal, not a market signal — so when a proposal lands, check the licence, product approvals and past FDA actions; if there is any seizure history, ask for the closure order before sanction.** The one large local commitment is Mother Dairy's Rs 525 crore Nagpur dairy plant, part of a Rs 750 crore programme [3] — but that article is dated March 2024, so treat it as old news and collect current status from the customer.

## Where to grow, and how
Pursue frozen and snack processors with domestic retail contracts and diversified buyers — peer frozen volumes grew about 39% YoY in Q2 FY26 [6], and snacks and pulp are described as showing strong growth with capacity expansion underway [7]. **Avoid plain pulp exporters with single-market dependence and traders without own processing.** Structure on receivables and inventory, not on land. **Take stock and receivable statements every month, and a buyer-wise sales register every quarter; if a single buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for the contract.**

## Early warning signs
- Monthly stock statement versus sanctioned drawing power (monthly): shortfall beyond 10% -> freeze further drawing and inspect godown. - FDA or licensing action (event-based): any seizure or show-cause -> stop enhancement and obtain closure order [1]. - Raw material price versus contracted selling price (quarterly): margin compression -> reset limits to cash cycle.
